questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant courses, good university, within Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses and exams were very difficult and stressful. There was no preparation time the days before exams, no break after exams and no vacations during fall, so I had zero days off. The professors had very high expectations, even for short courses. As a hardworking student, I barely passed my exams and I was very stressed the entire period. I did enjoy the culture and the friends I made.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived after the welcome meeting, so I had a private meeting with the exchange office adviser. She was very kind and helpful during my entire exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have liked more social events the first few weeks to meet other students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult finding housing, and I almost didn't manage to find anything before starting my studies. I joined multiple Facebook groups and wrote endless messages to people renting out rooms, and suddenly I got lucky. Also, housing is very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult finding housing in Amsterdam, even if you are starting to look long before moving. The transport is also quite expensive if you find something far away from the campus. I wish you good luck!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student housing was very limited. I didn't manage to get housing, not even a spot on the wait list.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had an online platform where you could register and deregister courses. Easy to use.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance counselors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to register for a specific course that was mandatory for my track at my home university, but I was not allowed as it was technically a bachelor course at the host university and I was a master student. Otherwise I was able to register for all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No specific advice, it was very simple.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All courses were MA level, and I was not allowed to take BA level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar with lectures, seminars and assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Particle Physics 1, General Relativity for Astrophysics, Cosmology, Extreme Astrophysics, Advanced Cosmology

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Particle Physics 1, Cosmology, Extreme Astrophysics and Advanced Cosmology are good courses for astro and particle physics, although difficult. The professors are capable and the content is interesting. The exams are difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was much more expensive than expected, and transport was also more expensive that expected. Food and other living costs were as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds I imagine, but I had no time for extra activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't have time to participate in any activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Amsterdam city by visiting museums, doing a walking tour or canal cruise, eating local food. Also visiting nearby cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture was very similar to the culture of my home country, so it was quite easy to adjust. Still fun to learn about a new culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people you take the same courses as and meet the friends of your friends. Be open and kind.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The canals, museums, markets and the people. How Amsterdam is small and cozy compared to other huge capitals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for the housing crisis: start looking early and bring all the grants you can get. The studying is hard and stressful, so remember to take your own breaks and enjoy the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Finding housing is really difficult.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made, and hopefully keep in touch with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses and exams, which I barely passed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
